the percentage of glycosylation of the hemoglobin in the blood of food-restricted rats is significantly lower than that in ad libitum-fed rats.
food restriction in rats results in a lower percentage of hemoglobin glycosylation and a lower plasma glucose concentration than in ad libitum rats.

food restriction of rats results in a sustained decrease in plasma glucose concentration and in the percentage glycosylation (glycated hemoglobin) of hemoglobin, which provides support for the glycaton hypothesis of aging.

the role of glucose in the aging process.
